name: Data Center Capacity
description: Size the market for enterprise data center capacity.
formula: TAM = Population x Penetration_rate x Purchase_frequency x Average_spend
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify addressable population = target_population x addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply penetration rate = addressable_population x penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate annual spend per user = purchase_frequency x avg_spend_per_purchase
Step 4: Calculate TAM = penetrating_users x annual_spend_per_user
key_insight: Market sizing is about defensible assumptions, not precision. Show your logic clearly -- the interviewer is testing your structure, not your arithmetic.
common_mistakes: Sizing the total population instead of the addressable segment
Forgetting purchase frequency -- confusing annual vs per-transaction spend
Not sanity-checking the output against known benchmarks
framework_soundbite: Top-down or bottom-up -- pick one, state your assumptions, and sanity-check the output. The logic matters more than the number.
business_contexts: a cloud infrastructure provider evaluating a new data center region
a private equity fund sizing demand for colocation capacity
question_patterns: A cloud infrastructure provider is deciding whether to open a new regional data center and wants to size annual demand from mid-market enterprises.

prompts.beginner: Estimate the total addressable market for enterprise data center colocation capacity.
prompts.intermediate: A cloud infrastructure provider is deciding whether to open a new regional data center and wants to size annual demand from mid-market enterprises.
prompts.advanced: An infrastructure fund is evaluating a colocation operator whose growth story depends on enterprise capacity demand the fund's own technical advisors are divided on. Build an independent size-of-market view before the investment committee meets.
